questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Rarely a company has achieved such rapid market dominance.
Rarely has a company achieved such rapid market dominance.
Rarely does a company achieved such rapid market dominance.
Rarely a company achieves such rapid market dominance has.
questions.explanation: Negative adverbials like 'rarely' at the start trigger inversion: 'Rarely has a company achieved...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: It is essential that the board approves the merger by Friday.
It is essential that the board approve the merger by Friday.
It is essential that the board will approve the merger by Friday.
It is essential that the board approving the merger by Friday.
questions.explanation: After 'it is essential that', formal English uses the subjunctive (base form): 'the board approve the merger.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Were it not for the sudden currency devaluation, the company would have thrived.
Were it not the sudden currency devaluation, the company would have thrived.
Was it not for the sudden currency devaluation, the company would have thrived.
Were it not for the sudden currency devaluation, the company will have thrived.
questions.explanation: 'Were it not for' is a formal inverted conditional meaning 'if it weren't for': 'Were it not for the devaluation, the company would have thrived.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The startup secured funding, albeit a smaller amount than expected.
The startup secured funding, albeit that a smaller amount than expected.
The startup secured funding, albeit it a smaller amount than expected.
The startup secured funding albeit for a smaller amount than expected.
questions.explanation: 'Albeit' introduces a concession and is typically followed directly by a noun phrase or adjective: 'albeit a smaller amount.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: It was the CFO who first identified the accounting discrepancy.
It was the CFO which first identified the accounting discrepancy.
It was the CFO whom first identified the accounting discrepancy.
It the CFO was who first identified the accounting discrepancy.
questions.explanation: Cleft sentences for emphasis on a person use 'It was [person] who...': 'It was the CFO who first identified...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The economist contends that inflation will ease by next quarter.
The economist contends to that inflation will ease by next quarter.
The economist contends inflation will easing by next quarter.
The economist is contend that inflation will ease by next quarter.
questions.explanation: 'Contend' (formal reporting verb meaning 'argue') is followed by 'that + clause': 'contends that inflation will ease.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Having reviewed the quarterly figures, the board decided to postpone the acquisition.
Having review the quarterly figures, the board decided to postpone the acquisition.
Have reviewed the quarterly figures, the board decided to postpone the acquisition.
Having reviewed the quarterly figures, the board deciding to postpone the acquisition.
questions.explanation: 'Having + past participle' shows a completed action before the main clause: 'Having reviewed the figures, the board decided...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The vast majority of shareholders has voted in favor of the merger.
The vast majority of shareholders have voted in favor of the merger.
A vast majority of shareholders is voted in favor of the merger.
The vast majority of shareholders vote in favor of the merger already.
questions.explanation: 'The majority of' + plural noun typically takes a plural verb: 'the vast majority of shareholders have voted.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The firm needn't have laid off so many employees; the crisis passed quickly.
The firm needn't laid off so many employees; the crisis passed quickly.
The firm didn't need have laid off so many employees; the crisis passed quickly.
The firm needn't have lay off so many employees; the crisis passed quickly.
questions.explanation: 'Needn't have + past participle' expresses an unnecessary past action: 'needn't have laid off so many employees.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Not only did revenue increase, but profit margins also improved.
Not only revenue increased, but profit margins also improved.
Not only did revenue increase, but also profit margins improved.
Not only revenue did increase, but profit margins also improved.
questions.explanation: 'Not only' at the start of a clause triggers inversion: 'Not only did revenue increase, but profit margins also improved.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The merger is arguably the most significant deal in the industry's history.
The merger is arguable the most significant deal in the industry's history.
The merger arguably is the most significant deal in the industry's history it.
The merger is arguably that the most significant deal in the industry's history.
questions.explanation: 'Arguably' is an adverb used to hedge a strong claim: 'the merger is arguably the most significant deal.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The company introduced a scheme whereby employees can buy shares at a discount.
The company introduced a scheme where employees can buy shares at a discount by.
The company introduced a scheme by which whereby employees can buy shares.
The company introduced a scheme whereby that employees can buy shares at a discount.
questions.explanation: 'Whereby' means 'by which' and introduces a formal relative clause describing a process: 'a scheme whereby employees can buy shares.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: So severe was the downturn that several major banks collapsed.
So severe the downturn was that several major banks collapsed.
So severe was the downturn several major banks collapsed.
So severe was that the downturn several major banks collapsed.
questions.explanation: Fronting 'so + adjective' for emphasis triggers inversion: 'So severe was the downturn that several banks collapsed.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The restructuring of the company's debt eased investor concerns considerably.
The restructure of the company's debt eased investor concerns considerably.
The restructuring of the company's debt ease investor concerns considerably.
The restructuring the company's debt eased investor concerns considerably.
questions.explanation: Formal writing nominalizes verbs: 'restructure' becomes 'the restructuring of...'

questions.topic: Passive with modal perfect (could have been)
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The losses could have been avoided if management had acted sooner.
The losses could been avoided if management had acted sooner.
The losses could have avoided if management had acted sooner.
The losses could have being avoided if management had acted sooner.
questions.explanation: Modal perfect passive: modal + have been + past participle: 'could have been avoided.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Some analysts expect a recession; others, a soft landing.
Some analysts expect a recession; others expect, a soft landing.
Some analysts expect a recession; others is a soft landing.
Some analysts expect a recession; others expects a soft landing.
questions.explanation: Ellipsis omits the repeated verb after a semicolon: 'others, a soft landing' (= others expect a soft landing).

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Profits fell sharply. Nevertheless, the CEO remained optimistic.
Profits fell sharply, nevertheless the CEO remained optimistic.
Profits fell sharply. Nevertheless the CEO remained optimistic.
Profits fell sharply nevertheless, the CEO remained optimistic.
questions.explanation: 'Nevertheless' begins a new sentence and is followed by a comma: 'Profits fell sharply. Nevertheless, the CEO remained optimistic.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Notwithstanding the setbacks, the company posted record profits.
Notwithstanding of the setbacks, the company posted record profits.
Notwithstanding the setbacks, but the company posted record profits.
The setbacks notwithstanding of, the company posted record profits.
questions.explanation: 'Notwithstanding' is a formal preposition meaning 'despite' and is followed directly by a noun phrase: 'Notwithstanding the setbacks...'

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate formal opening line for an email requesting a meeting with a potential investor?
options: I'm writing to see if you wanna meet up sometime.
I am writing to request a meeting at your earliest convenience to discuss a potential partnership.
Hey, can we meet? I have a business idea.
Just wondering if you're free to chat about a deal.
questions.explanation: 'I am writing to request a meeting at your earliest convenience...' is a standard formal opening for professional correspondence.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate opening line for a formal complaint about a breached contract?
options: I'm super annoyed that you broke our contract.
I am writing to draw your attention to a breach of contract on the part of your company.
You broke the contract, and I want to complain.
I am writing to draw your attention to a breach of contract on the part of your company, ok.
questions.explanation: Formal complaints use precise, measured language such as 'I am writing to draw your attention to a breach of contract...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The two firms met to iron out the details of the merger.
The two firms met to iron the details out of the merger.
The two firms met to iron the details of the merger out.
The two firms met to iron out of the details of the merger.
questions.explanation: 'Iron out' means 'to resolve' and is commonly used with 'details': 'iron out the details of the merger.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The proposal got rejected by the board after a lengthy debate.
The proposal got reject by the board after a lengthy debate.
The proposal got rejecting by the board after a lengthy debate.
The proposal was got rejected by the board after a lengthy debate.
questions.explanation: Informal/semi-formal passive with 'get': get + past participle: 'the proposal got rejected by the board.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: All things considered, the acquisition was a sound business decision.
All things consider, the acquisition was a sound business decision.
All things considering, the acquisition was a sound business decision.
All things considered that, the acquisition was a sound business decision.
questions.explanation: 'All things considered' is a fixed absolute participle phrase meaning 'taking everything into account.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: In light of the recent scandal, the CEO stepped down.
In the light of the recent scandal, the CEO stepped down, that.
Light of the recent scandal, the CEO stepped down.
In light for the recent scandal, the CEO stepped down.
questions.explanation: 'In light of' means 'considering' and is followed by a noun phrase: 'In light of the recent scandal...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The investment yielded a substantial profit within two years.
The investment made a substantial profit yield within two years.
The investment gave a substantial profit yield within two years.
The investment yielded of a substantial profit within two years.
questions.explanation: 'Yield a profit' is a fixed collocation meaning 'to produce a profit': 'the investment yielded a substantial profit.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The committee has consistently maintained a cautious approach to investment.
The committee has maintained consistently a cautious approach to investment.
Consistently the committee has maintained a cautious approach to investment.
The committee consistently has maintained a cautious approach to investment.
questions.explanation: Adverbs of frequency in formal writing typically follow the auxiliary verb: 'has consistently maintained.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The market is highly volatile. Furthermore, regulatory changes add uncertainty.
The market is highly volatile, furthermore regulatory changes add uncertainty.
The market is highly volatile. Furthermore regulatory changes add uncertainty.
The market is highly volatile furthermore, regulatory changes add uncertainty.
questions.explanation: 'Furthermore' begins a new sentence and is followed by a comma: 'The market is volatile. Furthermore, regulatory changes add uncertainty.'

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag.
options: The board would rarely approve such a risky deal, would they?
The board would rarely approve such a risky deal, wouldn't they?
The board would rarely approve such a risky deal, don't they?
The board would rarely approve such a risky deal, do they?
questions.explanation: 'Rarely' makes the statement effectively negative, so the tag is positive: 'would rarely approve..., would they?'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The results were not entirely satisfactory.
The results were not all satisfactory entirely.
The results not were entirely satisfactory.
The results were entirely not satisfactory.
questions.explanation: Formal understatement places 'not' before the adverb: 'The results were not entirely satisfactory.'

questions.topic: Advanced conditionals (Had it not been for)
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Had it not been for the emergency loan, the company would have gone bankrupt.
Had it not for the emergency loan, the company would have gone bankrupt.
Had it not been the emergency loan, the company would have gone bankrupt.
Had it not been for the emergency loan, the company will have gone bankrupt.
questions.explanation: 'Had it not been for' is a formal inverted past conditional meaning 'if it hadn't been for': 'Had it not been for the loan, the company would have gone bankrupt.'
